extracted.intended_audience: home dressmakers, milliners and fashionable readers; also music teachers and amateur musicians
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and stylistic rules for late-19th-century women's dressmaking, millinery and pattern use, plus short evaluative notes for new music and pedagogical manuals. Includes construction details, trimming advice, and pattern instructions intended for home makers and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: No trains except for court/older evening gowns
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no trains to any dresses, whatever people may say—save and except to court dresses and the evening gowns worn by a few dowagers who fancy old ways the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat trains as exceptional; day and general evening wear should avoid trains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silhouette: give length and height
rubrics_metrics.description: The general idea with reference to all draperies, overskirts, panels, and skirts is to give length and height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose drapery and paneling to lengthen the figure; tall women should choose skirts carefully so as not to look 'too gigantic.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Material combinations by dress type
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the morning dresses are made of two woollen materials; a better kind of walking or afternoon dress with a woollen and silk material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use heavier wools for mornings and mixed wool/silk for walking/afternoon; mix fancy silks with woollens as trimming/underskirts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skirt width and support (tournure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The skirts are generally rather wider, but are not distended, except by a moderate tournure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wider skirts are acceptable only when moderated by a moderate tournure; avoid excessive distension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching trims: collars, cuffs and revers
rubrics_metrics.description: The collar, cuffs, and revers are of the same material as the underskirt, and bands of this material are put round the edge of the overskirt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent trim material across collar, cuffs, revers and overskirt edging for coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaids/cut on the bias and use of folds
rubrics_metrics.description: When this is a plaid it is cut on the bias, and with plaids folds are very much used everywhere that they can be introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut plaids on the bias to get better fall and employ folds to integrate plaids into drapery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleeve styles and treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evening sleeves: puffs of thin material from the shoulders to the elbow, ending in a plain band of velvet, or a puff of transparent material at the elbow; some sleeves have puffs inside the arm at the elbow; daytime deep cuffs stand away like cavalier glove cuffs; puffs at the shoulder; new sleeve with no seam at the back of the arm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select sleeve type appropriate to occasion; combine puffs, bands, and deep cuffs as described; consider Venetian portraiture influences for shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoulder-straps and epaulettes
rubrics_metrics.description: Shoulder-straps and epaulettes are very popular additions to the bodice; and we find shoulder-straps without epaulettes, and epaulettes without shoulder-straps, or both together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shoulder-straps and/or epaulettes as decorative or structural elements; they may be of the dress material and braided or embroidered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: bodice imitating a railway porter's waistcoat
rubrics_metrics.description: One bodice ... both ugly and peculiar, ... a faithful copy of a railway porter’s waistcoat—with its front of corduroy, and its back of linen... In the copy, the fronts are of velvet, fancy or plain plush, and the backs are of plain silk ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incongruous combinations that mimic utilitarian menswear (front/back mismatch) — treated as an ugly/peculiar design example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trimming and economical repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodices are a great deal trimmed at present. ... The sleeves are often trimmed round the shoulder-seams on the bodice—a very useful fashion indeed, as the sides, which are too well worn by the friction of the arms, can be made quite respectable for a longer term of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use trimming strategically to refresh or extend the life of garments (e.g., cover worn areas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basque and bodice cutting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The basques are all cut very short on the hips, and are generally ended in a square-cut tail at the back, with a fan of pleats, or even plain, and not with ornaments at all. The darts in front are cut very high, and are straight in form; and there are two side pieces—one quite below the arm; and the seam of the side piece at the back is as straightly cut as possible. The great fancy is still for a narrow and flat back, and all methods of cutting out tried to produce this effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct basques with short hip cut, high straight darts, and straightly cut side/back seams to achieve a narrow, flat back silhouette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mantle/cloak shape and alteration guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mantles ... are short at the back and long in front, the ends being either square or pointed. ... Ulsters are usually made of checked woollens, though they are by no means 'loud' in tone. ... The long jackets will be found to cut into shape very well; and I have recently helped to alter a paletôt ... cutting it up nearly to the waist, at the back, and into deep square ends in front. The trimming then laid on was black astrachan ... making it quite a new garment at a very small expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor short-back/long-front mantles; check ulsters subtly; practical alteration can renew garments cheaply — offer concrete trimming examples and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collars: pleated satin as modern replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of the almost forgotten sets of linen collars and cuffs, many ladies are wearing pleated satin, the pleats being very close and small. The satin is used in various colours, and appears also in the necks and sleeves of evening dresses, especially in black ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pleated satin collars as fashionable, colorful alternatives to linen sets; suits black evening dresses well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Millinery: minimal trimming and construction tips
rubrics_metrics.description: So little trimming is placed on bonnets that it is quite worth while to manufacture them at home ... Care must be taken to set the bows in front up well, and, if a soft material, a long bit of wire will form a support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home millinery is feasible when trimming is minimal; use wire supports for soft bows to set them neatly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessories: preferred flowers and pocket form
rubrics_metrics.description: The flower of the day is the white chrysanthemum ... Very few flowers, however, are seen in millinery, and ribbons seem in greater favour. A new idea in the way of dress pockets is to have the pocket made as a little gathered bag or reticule, which hangs at the side for the handkerchief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor ribbons over floral millinery; adopt small gathered reticule-style pockets for practicality and fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stockings and footwear: self-colour and lacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The stockings produced for wearing this winter are quiet and ladylike-looking, being self-coloured, to match any dress ... The newest shoes all appear to lace, not button ... Laced boots are also returning to favour ... always try to keep a spare lace in the house, in case of breakages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose self-coloured stockings and laced footwear for neatness and fit; keep spare laces to maintain a tidy appearance and avoid untidy wear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fur accessories: compact muffs with purse and sensible handles
rubrics_metrics.description: The new winter muffs of fur are not large, and nearly all of them are supplied with a purse or pocket of some kind, and also have handles of fur, which are more convenient than the purse; for the muff can be slung over the arm when shopping, or when it is necessary to keep the hands free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer smaller, functional muffs with pockets and handles for convenience rather than impractical long cords; caution about excessively suggestive trim (legs on boas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper pattern sizing and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: All paper patterns supplied by 'The Lady Dressmaker' are of medium size, viz., thirty-six inches round the chest, and only one size is prepared for sale. No turnings are allowed in any of them. Each pattern may be had ... price 1s. each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect single-size medium patterns (36" chest) without seam allowances/turnings; plan adjustments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norfolk blouse pattern construction specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Norfolk jacket ... consists of seven pieces: the front, back, collar, belt, two halves of a sleeve, and a cuff. The back should be cut double, as there is no join down the centre; a deep hem must be allowed on each side the front where the buttons are placed; the pleats turn forward, and the position of the notches should be very carefully observed. The edges may be finished by a row of machine stitching, which should be even and good. No lining is needed ... quantity of material required ... about three yards and a half of thirty-six inches in width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow pattern-piece list exactly; cut back double; allow deep hems for buttons; run pleats forward; finish edges with even machine stitching; use ~3.5 yards of 36" material; no seams allowed in pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norfolk blouse with yoke (nine-piece) assembly notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The other blouse is made with a yoke, and has nine pieces, viz., front, back, two sleeve pieces, collar, cuff, belt, and two yoke pieces, back and front. In cutting out, the back must be cut double, and in making up the yoke should be stitched flatly on the pleated portions with the machine before joining the bodice together. Both the belts should be lined with buckram, and machine-stitched at each edge, to render them firm and useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making yoke version, stitch yoke flat onto pleated sections before joining; line belts with buckram and machine-stitch edges for firmness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended materials for the Norfolk blouses
rubrics_metrics.description: The materials used are elastic cloth, serge, diagonal, blue linen, cashmere, and, of course, any dress material which may be in fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose from recommended durable and suitable fabrics for blouses; select according to intended wear and fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edge finishing and machine stitching standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The edges may be finished by a row of machine stitching, which should be even and good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure neat, even machine stitching for finished edges — a mark of good construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fashion column voice: practical, economical advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice emphasises making and altering garments at small expense and making older garments serviceable by trimming/alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise economical alterations and trimming to update garments rather than expensive replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting text mood in song composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A sympathetic, easy setting of the sad words by Helen M. Waitman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting lyrics, aim for settings that sympathetically reflect the mood of the words; ease of delivery is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompaniment: need for contrast and rests
rubrics_metrics.description: The violin accompaniment, charming as it is, would have been much more so, had it been broken up a little more. There is no rest for it, and this destroys much of its effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unrelenting accompaniment; introduce rests and breaks to create contrast and enhance effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal range suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The song is within the compass of most singers—C to D, and not higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose/vet songs with accessible vocal compass to suit intended performers; indicate ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for student/adolescent parts (violin fingerings/bows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two Melodies ... are intended for young people ... we are surprised that the violin part is neither fingered nor bowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For youth/student pieces include fingering and bowing indications to aid learning and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical usefulness of pedagogical collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Arpeggios.—An extremely useful collection of these technical passages. ... The arrangement of the arpeggios is founded on the well-known work of Charles Chaulieu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical collections for usefulness and sound pedagogical lineage; arrangements that mirror established methods are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustaining excitement and structural drive
rubrics_metrics.description: Tarantella ... A very characteristic specimen of this frenzied dance. The excitement is well sustained to the close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure pieces that rely on excitement maintain energy and structural drive through to the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of local colouring/character
rubrics_metrics.description: Violanté ... containing what Mr. Corder would call 'distinct local colouring,' and developing a graceful subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local or national colour judiciously to give character to a piece without sacrificing melodic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical method: graded steps and balanced theory/practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Child Pianist, divided into grades and steps, and combining in a thoughtful and systematic way a little theory and a little practice, never forcing a child, and never letting the head get in front of the hands or vice versâ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective methods are graded, balance theory and practice, avoid forcing the child, and maintain coordination between intellectual understanding and physical ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include pupil-teacher duets and teacher guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanying these steps with their capital duets for pupil and teacher, ... we have a Teacher's Guide to the Child Pianist, an assistance to young teachers, and an essential explanation to the exercises and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide duet material for pedagogy and a teacher's guide explaining exercises/method to support inexperienced teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical tone: care and management
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot too highly estimate the care and management displayed by Mrs. J. S. Curwen, the authoress of these valuable works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate method books on demonstrated care and sensible management in structuring progress and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pedal overuse on organ pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Two Andantes ... the pedals are used without intermission from beginning to end, augmenting a want of contrast and variety already too apparent in both pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use organ pedals judiciously; continuous pedal can reduce contrast and variety — aim for restraint to preserve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility across keys is a merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Yellow Roses we can recommend as a pretty ballad by Michael Watson. It is published in every necessary key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing songs in all common keys increases accessibility for different voice types and is a positive attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs conventionality in popular songs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Old See-Saw is a song of the conventional 'Swing, swing' type, but brightly written, and likely to add to ... reputation as a popular writer of small things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional forms are acceptable when well-written and bright; originality is desirable but craft in familiar types is also appreciated.
